newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Armed Albanians try to hijack Greek passenger boat.
newsitem.headline: Armed Albanians try to hijack Greek passenger boat.

text.p: Albanian gunmen briefly hijacked a small Greek passenger boat in a desperate bid to reach Italy on Sunday but were stopped by armed locals who turned them back, eyewitnesses said.
"About 20 armed Albanians boarded the Kalliope and forced the captain to sail off at gunpoint," said a Greek reporter who had just arrived on the boat.

When news of the hijack reached the town, about 10 armed locals boarded two speedboats and went after the ship, the only regular link between the Greek island of Corfu and the troubled Balkan country, and forced it to return, she told Reuters.

The small passenger ferry had just dropped off passengers and supplies to this southern Albanian port before being hijacked, a Reuters cameraman said. There were no passengers on the ship during the incident.
The Kalliope was still in Sarande. The port authority on Corfu told Reuters efforts to reach the ship by radio had failed and they were not sure when it would return to the island.
"The locals freed the gunmen, who said they did it because they were destitute and desperate to get to Italy," the reporter said.
The Kalliope has been this area's lifeline, delivering food and medicine since rebels took over most major southern Albanian towns, plunging them into anarchy.

Many Albanians who lost their life's savings in a string of fraudulent pyramid schemes have begun to flee across the Adriatic Sea to Italy but so far there has been no mass movement towards the long Greek border with Albania.
Rebel councils in the south have been trying to restore some order and stop gangs, armed to the teeth from looted army arsenals, from roaming and terrorising the region.
Reporters in the southern town of Gjirocaster said locals were seen repairing the burned police stations and policemen were wearing their uniforms again.
